title: Week 21 Mastery Quiz · Diplomacy, Negotiation, and Statecraft

questions.question: Article 33 of the UN Charter names several peaceful dispute mechanisms. Which interpretation suits a negotiation briefing?
options: All disputes must go first to the ICJ.
Parties have a range of peaceful methods to pursue and must assess suitability for the dispute.
Negotiation is forbidden once mediation begins.
The Charter guarantees agreement within one year.
questions.explanation: Parties have a range of peaceful methods to pursue and must assess suitability for the dispute.

questions.question: Fictional maritime talks: A requests a 60-mile zone, B offers 30, and both accept 45 in principle. What further issue determines durability?
options: Which minister speaks first.
Whether each side uses identical slogans.
A verifiable boundary definition and compliance process.
Whether the negotiation lasted an even number of days.
questions.explanation: A verifiable boundary definition and compliance process.

questions.question: A mediator privately receives contradictory maps from two parties. What procedure best protects negotiation integrity?
options: Publish one map as proven without review.
Discard both maps regardless of origin.
Treat political endorsements as geographic measurements.
Establish provenance, coordinate systems and agreed factual verification before bargaining from disputed maps.
questions.explanation: Establish provenance, coordinate systems and agreed factual verification before bargaining from disputed maps.

questions.question: One party threatens to abandon talks unless a separate tariff question is discussed. What is the analytical name for this tactic?
options: Issue linkage, whose effects on bargaining depend on leverage and interests.
Automatic arbitration.
Judicial precedent.
A treaty reservation made after ratification.
questions.explanation: Issue linkage, whose effects on bargaining depend on leverage and interests.

questions.question: A ceasefire document states monitoring begins 'soon' but provides no inspection authority. What is the best revision?
options: Increase ceremonial signatures.
Define dates, authorized monitors, data access, verification and response to alleged breaches.
Remove the timetable entirely.
State that verification is unnecessary when both parties sign.
questions.explanation: Define dates, authorized monitors, data access, verification and response to alleged breaches.

questions.question: A delegate believes its minimum acceptable settlement is 40 units but publicly demands 70. What should a researcher distinguish?
options: Official demand from legally binding treaty law.
Negotiation from all communication.
Opening position from reservation point, without assuming either is fully observable.
A public speech from independent polling.
questions.explanation: Opening position from reservation point, without assuming either is fully observable.

questions.question: A negotiation memorandum quotes only government statements to prove civilian support. What evidence is still required?
options: A second government speech.
The number of countries mentioned in the memorandum.
A map with no population data.
Representative or appropriately bounded public evidence and analysis of who is excluded.
questions.explanation: Representative or appropriately bounded public evidence and analysis of who is excluded.

questions.question: An envoy reports a handshake deal although neither team has authority to ratify it. Which risk is most relevant?
options: A gap between informal agreement and legally authorized adoption or implementation.
A treaty necessarily entered into force.
Public announcement overrides domestic approval rules.
A signed photograph proves enforcement capacity.
questions.explanation: A gap between informal agreement and legally authorized adoption or implementation.

questions.question: A fictional peace proposal creates a joint inspection team funded by only one side. What governance question is most important?
options: Whether the team's logo is bilingual.
Whether financing, appointment and access rules protect the team's impartiality and credibility.
Whether inspectors wear uniforms.
Whether talks occurred in the same building.
questions.explanation: Whether financing, appointment and access rules protect the team's impartiality and credibility.

questions.question: After an agreement, border incidents drop but independent reporting also declines. Which conclusion is warranted?
options: Violence necessarily ended.
The agreement itself proves peace.
Reported incidents declined; without comparable monitoring, actual incident trends remain uncertain.
Fewer reports establish complete compliance.
questions.explanation: Reported incidents declined; without comparable monitoring, actual incident trends remain uncertain.

shortResponse: How can actors negotiate durable agreements when interests, power, information, and trust differ?
rubric: 10 points: precise claim (2), accurate concepts (2), two specific pieces of evidence (2), reasoning (2), counterargument or limitation (1), revision condition (1).
